// diagnostic

L2401

Public function `{fn}` has a positional `Bool` parameter `{param}`.

What

Public function `{fn}` has a positional `Bool` parameter `{param}`.

Why

Positional booleans are easy to transpose: `connect(host, true, false)` is a guessing game. Labels (S61) make the intent clear at the call site.

Fix

Callers can use `{param}: true` to document intent; or give the parameter a default value so it can be omitted. No action required — this is advisory.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning L2401: tests/ui_lint/l2401_method_bool.warn.

Warning [L2401] (positional_bool_parameter): public method `listen` has a positional `Bool` parameter `blocking`
  --> tests/ui_lint/l2401_method_bool.jet:6:25
    |
  6 |     pub fn listen(self, blocking: Bool) Int -> 0
    |                         ^^^^^^^^
 Why: positional booleans are easy to transpose at the call site
 Fix: callers can write `blocking: true` to make the intent clear (S61 labels)
More: jet-lang.dev/e/L2401

Warning [L0102] (unused_parameter): parameter `blocking` is never used.
  --> tests/ui_lint/l2401_method_bool.jet:6:25
    |
  6 |     pub fn listen(self, blocking: Bool) Int -> 0
    |                         ^^^^^^^^
 Why: an unused parameter often means the function contract or implementation is incomplete; Jet keeps this warning-only so prototypes stay unblocked.
 Fix: use `blocking`, rename it to `_blocking` when it is intentionally unused, or remove it from the function contract.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/L0102
